grammarQuestions.subtopic: Future Perfect Continuous & Time Clauses
grammarQuestions.stem: By the time the international consortium ---- the subterranean neutrino observatory late next decade, theoretical astrophysicists ---- competing models of solar core fusion for nearly a century.
cues: By the time + Present Simple
late next decade (future point)
for nearly a century (duration up to future point)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Uluslararası konsorsiyum önümüzdeki on yılın sonlarında yeraltı nötrino gözlemevini devreye alana kadar, teorik astrofizikçiler yaklaşık bir asırdır güneş çekirdeği füzyonunun rakip modellerini geliştirmekte olacaklar.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'By the time' zaman bağlacı, gelecek zaman referansı ('late next decade') içerdiğinde yan cümlecikte Present Simple veya Present Perfect ('commissions'), ana cümlecikte ise gelecekteki bir noktaya kadar süregelen eylem vurgusu ('for nearly a century') bulunduğundan Future Perfect Continuous ('will have been refining') gerektirir. Zaman bağlaçlarının bulunduğu yan cümlecikte 'will' kesinlikle kullanılmaz.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: When a 'By the time' clause refers to the future ('late next decade'), the time clause takes the Present Simple ('commissions') rather than 'will'. Because the main clause includes the duration marker 'for nearly a century' culminating at that future point, the Future Perfect Continuous ('will have been refining') is required.

distractorAnalysis.A: While 'has commissioned' is acceptable in a time clause, 'would have refined' expresses an unreal past conditional rather than a factual future timeline.
distractorAnalysis.B: Past tenses ('commissioned / had been refining') contradict the explicit future time marker 'late next decade'.
distractorAnalysis.C: Future auxiliary 'will commission' is grammatically forbidden inside a 'By the time' adverbial clause.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'will be refining' (Future Continuous) does not capture the cumulative hundred-year duration up to the completion point.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: Present Simple in the future time clause paired with Future Perfect Continuous for ongoing duration until a future reference point.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Past Perfect Continuous vs. Simple Past
grammarQuestions.stem: Although palaeoclimatologists ---- ice-core samples from the Antarctic plateau for over three decades, it was not until the advent of laser-ablation spectrometry that they ---- sub-decadal fluctuations in ancient atmospheric methane.
cues: for over three decades (prior to past milestone)
it was not until ... that (past milestone)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Paleoklimatologlar otuz yılı aşkın bir süredir Antarktika platosundan buz çekirdeği örnekleri çıkarıyor olmalarına rağmen, eski atmosferik metandaki on yıl altı dalgalanmaları ancak lazer ablasyon spektrometrisinin ortaya çıkışıyla tespit edebildiler.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İkinci cümlecikteki 'it was not until the advent of ... that' yapısı geçmişte gerçekleşmiş bir dönüm noktasını (Simple Past) anlatır. Bu geçmiş dönüm noktasından önceki 30 yıllık süreci ('for over three decades') ifade etmek için ilk boşlukta Past Perfect Continuous ('had been extracting'), ikinci boşlukta ise o geçmiş anda kazanılan başarıyı gösteren 'could detect' (was/were able to detect anlamında) kullanılmalıdır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The cleft structure 'it was not until... that' anchors the narrative in the past. An action in progress 'for over three decades' prior to that past breakthrough requires the Past Perfect Continuous ('had been extracting'), while the resulting past achievement takes 'could detect'.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'have been detecting' violates tense harmony with the past cleft construction.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'have detected' shifts illegitimately into the present despite the past cleft clause 'it was not until ... that'.
distractorAnalysis.C: Correct: 'had been extracting' marks the 30-year duration before the past milestone, and 'could detect' marks the resulting past capability.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'would extract' cannot express cumulative duration with 'for over three decades' before a specific past event.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'have been extracting' (Present Perfect Continuous) clashes with the past anchor 'it was not until', and 'had detected' reverses the chronological order.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Ever Since & Present Perfect Progression
grammarQuestions.stem: Ever since epigraphers ---- the bilingual cuneiform tablets excavated at Tell Fekheriye in 1979, historians of the Ancient Near East ---- the administrative autonomy of Neo-Assyrian vassal states.
cues: Ever since + Simple Past (in 1979)
Main clause: Present Perfect / Present Perfect Continuous
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Epigraflar 1979 yılında Tell Fekheriye'de kazılarak çıkarılan iki dilli çivi yazılı tabletleri deşifre ettiklerinden bu yana, Eski Yakın Doğu tarihçileri Yeni Asur vasal devletlerinin idari özerkliğini yeniden değerlendirmektedir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'Ever since' (o zamandan beri) bağlacının bulunduğu yan cümlecikte geçmişte belirli bir noktada ('in 1979') tamamlanmış eylem için Simple Past ('deciphered'), ana cümlecikte ise 1979'dan günümüze kadar devam eden akademik tartışma için Present Perfect Continuous ('have been re-evaluating') kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The time conjunction 'Ever since' coupled with the specific past timestamp 'in 1979' requires the Simple Past ('deciphered') in the subordinate clause and the Present Perfect Continuous ('have been re-evaluating') in the main clause.

distractorAnalysis.A: reverses the rule: the 'since' clause must be Simple Past (especially with 'in 1979'), and the main clause must be Present Perfect.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'would decipher' is inappropriate for a single dated historical event in 1979.
distractorAnalysis.C: Both clauses are locked in past tenses, ignoring the present relevance of 'Ever since'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'had deciphered' and 're-evaluated' fail to link the 1979 discovery to the present as required by 'Ever since'.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: 'Ever since + V2 (deciphered)' paired with 'have been V-ing (have been re-evaluating)' in the main clause.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Contrastive Time Frames (Up Until vs. Recent Years)
grammarQuestions.stem: Up until the late twentieth century, neurobiologists largely ---- that adult mammalian brains were incapable of generating new neurons; however, over the past two decades, empirical evidence ---- active neurogenesis in the hippocampus.
cues: Up until the late twentieth century (closed past era)
over the past two decades (up to now)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Yirminci yüzyılın sonlarına kadar nörobiyologlar yetişkin memeli beyinlerinin yeni nöronlar üretemeyeceğini büyük ölçüde varsayıyorlardı; ancak son yirmi yılda ampirik kanıtlar hipokampüste aktif nörogenezi doğrulamıştır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk cümlede 'Up until the late twentieth century' ifadesi artık sona ermiş geçmiş bir dönemi belirttiği için Simple Past ('assumed') gerektirir. İkinci cümlede ise 'over the past two decades' (son yirmi yılda - günümüze kadar uzanan süreç) zarfı Present Perfect ('has confirmed') kullanımını zorunlu kılar.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: 'Up until the late twentieth century' defines a completed past period requiring the Simple Past ('assumed'). Conversely, 'over the past two decades' bridges the past to the present moment, requiring the Present Perfect ('has confirmed').

distractorAnalysis.A: Correct: Simple Past for the closed historical period and Present Perfect for 'over the past two decades'.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'will have confirmed' introduces an unfounded future speculation.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'was confirming' (Past Continuous) clashes with 'over the past two decades', which includes the present.
distractorAnalysis.D: Reverses the required tenses: Present Perfect cannot be used with a closed past period ('the late twentieth century'), and Simple Past shouldn't pair with 'over the past two decades'.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'had confirmed' places the recent twenty-year findings into the distant past rather than the present.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Point-in-Past vs. Prior Completion
grammarQuestions.stem: When the Byzantine emissaries finally ---- the Tang imperial capital of Chang'an in 643 CE, silk-weaving guilds along the Tarim Basin ---- commercial monopolies over trans-Eurasian caravan routes for more than four centuries.
cues: When ... in 643 CE (specific past event)
for more than four centuries (duration prior to 643 CE)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Bizans elçileri MS 643 yılında Tang imparatorluk başkenti Chang'an'a nihayet ulaştıklarında, Tarim Havzası boyunca uzanan ipek dokuma loncaları dört asırdan fazla bir süredir Avrasya aşırı kervan yolları üzerinde ticari tekel uygulamaktaydılar.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'in 643 CE' net bir geçmiş zaman noktası olduğundan 'When' yan cümleciğinde Simple Past ('reached') kullanılır. MS 643 yılından önceki dört asırlık süreci ('for more than four centuries') vurgulamak için ana cümlecikte Past Perfect Continuous ('had been exercising') doğru seçimdir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The 'When' clause contains a specific historical date ('in 643 CE'), requiring the Simple Past ('reached'). The main clause describes an ongoing state that had lasted 'for more than four centuries' leading up to 643 CE, requiring the Past Perfect Continuous ('had been exercising').

distractorAnalysis.A: 'have reached' cannot co-occur with the explicit date 'in 643 CE'.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'have exercised' (Present Perfect) is incompatible with a 7th-century historical context.
distractorAnalysis.C: Reverses the chronological relationship by placing 'had reached' before 'exercised'.
distractorAnalysis.D: Correct: Simple Past for the 643 CE arrival and Past Perfect Continuous for the 400-year duration preceding it.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'would reach' does not fit a factual 'When' time clause anchored in 643 CE.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Future in the Past vs. Prior Subversion
grammarQuestions.stem: In the autumn of 1914, European ministries of finance ---- short-term war bonds on the assumption that hostilities would cease by Christmas, unaware that industrial attrition ---- any prospect of a swift armistice.
cues: In the autumn of 1914 (past narrative frame)
unaware that ... already (prior past completion)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: 1914 sonbaharında Avrupa maliye bakanlıkları, çatışmaların Noel'e kadar sona ereceği varsayımıyla kısa vadeli savaş tahvilleri çıkarıyorlardı; ancak endüstriyel yıpratma savaşının hızlı bir ateşkes olasılığını çoktan ortadan kaldırdığından habersizdiler.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'In the autumn of 1914' geçmiş zaman çerçevesinde o dönemde devam etmekte olan uygulamayı 'were issuing' (Past Continuous) anlatırken, 'unaware that ... already' ifadesi o tarihten önce çoktan gerçekleşmiş olan durumu Past Perfect ('had already eradicated') ile ifade eder.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: 'In the autumn of 1914' sets a past narrative frame where governments 'were issuing' bonds, while the noun clause following 'unaware that' with 'already' demands the Past Perfect ('had already eradicated') to mark prior completion.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'will have already eradicated' is a future perfect form that clashes with the 1914 setting.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'would issue' + 'was already eradicating' fails to capture the completed prior state indicated by 'already'.
distractorAnalysis.C: Correct: Past Continuous for the ongoing policy in autumn 1914 and Past Perfect for the prior reality that 'had already eradicated' peace prospects.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'have issued' violates the explicit past timestamp 'In the autumn of 1914'.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'has already eradicated' shifts ungrammatically to the present tense inside a past narrative.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Once + Present Perfect & Future Projection
grammarQuestions.stem: Once the European Space Agency ---- the interferometric laser antennas in heliocentric orbit in the 2030s, astrophysicists ---- gravitational ripples generated by supermassive black hole mergers across cosmic dawn.

options.A: has deployed / will be able to track

cues: Once (time conjunction)
in the 2030s (future horizon)
completion before future capability
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Avrupa Uzay Ajansı 2030'lu yıllarda interferometrik lazer antenlerini güneş merkezli yörüngeye yerleştirdiğinde, astrofizikçiler kozmik şafak boyunca süper kütleli kara delik birleşmelerinin ürettiği kütleçekimsel dalgalanmaları takip edebilecekler.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'Once' zaman bağlacı, gelecekteki bir zaman dilimini ('in the 2030s') işaret ettiğinde yan cümlecikte eylemin tamamlanmışlığını vurgulamak için Present Perfect ('has deployed') veya Present Simple alır; ana cümlecikte ise gelecekteki sonucu göstermek üzere 'will be able to track' kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: With the future time marker 'in the 2030s', the time conjunction 'Once' takes the Present Perfect ('has deployed') to emphasize completion of the deployment before the resulting future capability ('will be able to track').

distractorAnalysis.A: Correct: Present Perfect in the 'Once' time clause followed by 'will be able to track' in the main clause.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'deployed' (Simple Past) conflicts with the future time adverbial 'in the 2030s'.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'will deploy' is ungrammatical inside a time clause headed by 'Once'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'have been tracking' (Present Perfect Continuous) in the main clause contradicts the future dependency established by 'Once ... in the 2030s'.
distractorAnalysis.E: Past Perfect and 'would' describe counterfactual or past events, contradicting 'in the 2030s'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Geological Past vs. Anthropocene Present
grammarQuestions.stem: Whereas global sea levels ---- gradually in response to Milankovitch orbital cycles throughout the Pleistocene epoch, anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions ---- thermal expansion of the oceans at an unprecedented rate since the mid-twentieth century.
cues: throughout the Pleistocene epoch (completed geological epoch)
since the mid-twentieth century (up to present)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Küresel deniz seviyeleri Pleistosen çağı boyunca Milankovitch yörünge döngülerine tepki olarak kademeli biçimde dalgalanmışken, insan kaynaklı sera gazı emisyonları yirminci yüzyılın ortalarından bu yana okyanusların termal genleşmesini eşi benzeri görülmemiş bir hızla tetiklemektedir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'throughout the Pleistocene epoch' sona ermiş jeolojik bir dönemi ifade ettiğinden Simple Past ('fluctuated') gerektirir. Karşıtlık bağlacı ('Whereas') ile bağlanan ikinci cümlecikte ise 'since the mid-twentieth century' zarfı bulunduğundan Present Perfect Continuous ('have been driving') kullanılmalıdır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: 'throughout the Pleistocene epoch' refers to a closed geological era requiring the Simple Past ('fluctuated'). The second clause contains 'since the mid-twentieth century', requiring the Present Perfect Continuous ('have been driving').

distractorAnalysis.A: Inverts the required tenses: Present Perfect cannot describe the extinct Pleistocene epoch, nor can Simple Past pair with 'since the mid-twentieth century'.
distractorAnalysis.B: Correct: Simple Past for the completed Pleistocene epoch and Present Perfect Continuous for the ongoing trend since the mid-20th century.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'fluctuate' (Present Simple) mischaracterizes the past Pleistocene epoch.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'had driven' places the post-1950s phenomenon entirely in the past.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'were driving' fails to extend the action up to the present moment as demanded by 'since'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Negative Past Deduction vs. Unreal Past Consequence
grammarQuestions.stem: The Renaissance cartographers who drafted the 1507 Waldseemüller map ---- the Pacific Ocean through direct European reconnaissance, as Balboa did not cross the Isthmus of Panama until 1513; therefore, they ---- on mathematical extrapolations or unrecorded maritime accounts.

options.A: need not have charted / would have relied
options.B: must not have depicted / could rely
options.C: should not have depicted / might rely
options.D: may not have charted / should have relied
options.E: cannot have charted / must have relied

cues: did not cross ... until 1513 (impossibility in 1507)
therefore (logical past deduction)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: 1507 Waldseemüller haritasını çizen Rönesans haritacıları, Balboa 1513 yılına kadar Panama Kıstağı'nı geçmediği için Pasifik Okyanusu'nu doğrudan Avrupa keşifleriyle haritalandırmış olamazlar; dolayısıyla matematiksel çıkarımlara veya kayıt dışı denizcilik anlatılarına dayanmış olmalılar.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 1507'de çizilen bir haritada 1513'te keşfedilen okyanusun doğrudan gözlemle çizilmiş olması imkansızdır; geçmişe yönelik güçlü olumsuz çıkarım 'cannot have V3' ('cannot have charted') ile ifade edilir. İkinci boşlukta ise 'therefore' ile ulaşılan güçlü olumlu geçmiş çıkarım 'must have V3' ('must have relied') gerektirir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Because Balboa only reached the Pacific in 1513, it was impossible for the 1507 mapmakers to have charted it via direct European reconnaissance ('cannot have charted' = negative logical deduction about the past). Consequently, they 'must have relied' (strong affirmative past deduction) on other sources.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'need not have charted' means they did chart it unnecessarily, which contradicts historical fact.
distractorAnalysis.B: In formal English, negative past deduction of impossibility is expressed with 'cannot/couldn't have V3', and 'could rely' lacks past perfective aspect.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'should not have depicted' expresses criticism rather than logical impossibility, and 'might rely' fails to refer to the past.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'should have relied' implies an unfulfilled past obligation rather than a logical conclusion.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: 'cannot have charted' (past impossibility deduction) paired with 'must have relied' (strong affirmative past deduction).

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Needn't Have V3 vs. Could Have Been V3
grammarQuestions.stem: Subsequent metallurgical audits revealed that the municipal authority ---- the entire suspension bridge deck at such exorbitant cost, since the localized micro-fractures ---- through targeted cathodic protection alone.

options.A: need not have dismantled / could have been stabilized
options.B: ought not to dismantle / would have been stabilized
options.C: did not need to dismantle / must have been stabilized
options.D: cannot have dismantled / might have stabilized
options.E: must not have dismantled / should be stabilized

cues: at such exorbitant cost (action was actually performed)
since ... alone (alternative past possibility)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Sonraki metalurjik denetimler, bölgesel mikro çatlaklar yalnızca hedefli katodik koruma yoluyla stabilize edilebileceğinden, belediye idaresinin tüm asma köprü tabliyesini bu denli fahiş bir maliyetle sökmesine gerek olmadığını (ama boşuna söktüğünü) ortaya koydu.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'at such exorbitant cost' ifadesi köprü tabliyesinin gerçekten söküldüğünü, ancak sonradan yapılan denetimlerin bunun gereksiz olduğunu ortaya çıkardığını gösterir. Geçmişte yapılmış ancak gereksiz olduğu anlaşılan eylemler 'need not have V3' ('need not have dismantled') ile anlatılır. İkinci boşlukta ise gerçekleşmemiş geçmiş alternatif imkan edilgen yapıda 'could have been stabilized' ile verilir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The phrase 'at such exorbitant cost' confirms that the authority actually dismantled the deck, even though later audits showed it was unnecessary ('need not have dismantled'). The second blank requires the passive past possibility modal 'could have been stabilized'.

distractorAnalysis.A: Correct: 'need not have dismantled' (performed unnecessarily in the past) + 'could have been stabilized' (unactualized past passive possibility).
distractorAnalysis.B: 'ought not to dismantle' is present/future oriented, failing to capture the completed past expenditure.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'did not need to dismantle' typically implies the action was not performed, and 'must have been stabilized' asserts that stabilization actually occurred.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'might have stabilized' is active, whereas 'micro-fractures' is a passive subject.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'must not have dismantled' is a negative deduction, contradicting the fact that they incurred the exorbitant cost.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Unfulfilled Past Expectation (Was/Were to Have V3)
grammarQuestions.stem: The multilateral disarmament treaty ---- at the Geneva summit in May 1960; however, the diplomatic rapprochement collapsed overnight after a high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft was shot down over Soviet territory, which ---- a full-scale nuclear confrontation.

options.A: must have been ratified / should have precipitated
options.B: used to be ratified / would rather have precipitated
options.C: ought to be ratified / might have been precipitated
options.D: was to have been ratified / could easily have precipitated
options.E: would be ratified / had to precipitate

cues: collapsed overnight (plan was NOT fulfilled)
which ... (averted past danger)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Çok taraflı silahsızlanma antlaşmasının Mayıs 1960'taki Cenevre zirvesinde onaylanması planlanmıştı (ancak onaylanmadı); ne var ki yüksek irtifa keşif uçağının Sovyet toprakları üzerinde düşürülmesinin ardından diplomatik yakınlaşma bir gecede çöktü ki bu durum tam ölçekli bir nükleer çatışmayı kolayca tetikleyebilirdi.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'was/were to have V3' (edilgen: 'was to have been ratified') geçmişte resmi olarak planlanmış fakat beklenmedik bir engel yüzünden gerçekleşmemiş olayları anlatır. İkinci boşlukta ise geçmişte gerçekleşme ihtimali bulunan ancak ucuz atlatılan tehlike 'could easily have precipitated' ile ifade edilir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: 'was to have been ratified' expresses an official past arrangement that failed to materialize ('collapsed overnight'). The second blank uses 'could easily have precipitated' to denote a critical past danger that almost happened.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'must have been ratified' implies the treaty actually was ratified, contradicting 'the diplomatic rapprochement collapsed'.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'used to be ratified' and 'would rather have precipitated' are semantically nonsensical here.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'ought to be ratified' is present/future, and 'might have been precipitated' wrongly makes the relative clause passive despite having a direct object ('a full-scale nuclear confrontation').
distractorAnalysis.D: Correct: 'was to have been ratified' (unfulfilled past arrangement in passive voice) + 'could easily have precipitated' (unrealized past potential).
distractorAnalysis.E: 'had to precipitate' implies that a full-scale nuclear war actually took place.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Past Criticism (Ought to Have V3) & Emphatic Possibility (May Well Have V3)
grammarQuestions.stem: Epidemiological historians contend that quarantine officials in 1892 ---- municipal water filtration protocols weeks before the cholera outbreak peaked, as delays in chlorination ---- for nearly half of the preventable fatalities.

options.A: ought to have enforced / may well have accounted
options.B: need not have enforced / might account
options.D: had better enforce / can have accounted
options.E: would rather enforce / should have accounted

cues: in 1892 (past context)
preventable fatalities (criticism of past failure)
may well have V3 (strong past probability)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Epidemiyoloji tarihçileri, 1892'deki karantina yetkililerinin kolera salgını zirve yapmadan haftalar önce belediye su filtreleme protokollerini uygulamaya koymuş olmaları gerektiğini; zira klorlamadaki gecikmelerin önlenebilir ölümlerin yaklaşık yarısına yol açmış olabileceğini savunmaktadır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 1892 yılında yetkililerin yapması gereken ama yapmadığı bir görev eleştirisi söz konusu olduğundan 'ought to have enforced' (should have V3) kullanılır. İkinci boşlukta ise gecikmelerin ölümlerin yarısından sorumlu olma ihtimalini güçlü biçimde vurgulayan 'may well have accounted (for)' yapısı tam uyum sağlar.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Evaluating a past failure ('in 1892', 'preventable fatalities') requires 'ought to have enforced' (past obligation that was neglected). The second blank uses 'may well have accounted' to express a strong historical probability regarding the cause of deaths.

distractorAnalysis.A: Correct: 'ought to have enforced' (unfulfilled past duty) + 'may well have accounted' (strong past possibility).
distractorAnalysis.B: 'need not have enforced' claims filtration was unnecessary, contradicting 'preventable fatalities'.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'must account' is present tense and fails to refer back to the 1892 epidemic.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'had better enforce' is a present/future warning, and 'can have accounted' is ungrammatical in affirmative clauses.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'would rather enforce' is present preference, and 'should have accounted' absurdly suggests delays had a moral duty to cause fatalities.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Would Rather + Different Subject + Past Perfect
grammarQuestions.stem: Indigenous heritage councils across Polynesia have repeatedly stated that they would rather nineteenth-century colonial expeditions ---- ceremonial wooden carvings from ancestral shrines, demanding that European museums ---- these artifacts unconditionally.

options.E: have not confiscated / should have repatriated

cues: would rather + [different subject] + nineteenth-century (past time)
demanding that + [subject] + bare infinitive (subjunctive)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Polinezya genelindeki yerli miras konseyleri, 19. yüzyıl sömürge seferlerinin ata tapınaklarından törensel ahşap oymaları müsadere etmemiş olmasını tercih edeceklerini defalarca dile getirerek, Avrupa müzelerinin bu eserleri koşulsuz olarak iade etmesini talep etmektedir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'would rather' yapısından sonra yeni bir özne ('nineteenth-century colonial expeditions') geldiğinde ve geçmiş zamana ('nineteenth-century') atıf yapıldığında fiil Past Perfect ('had not confiscated') çekimlenir. İkinci kısımda ise 'demand that' subjunctive (istek kipi) tetikleyicisi olduğundan özne sonrasında yalın fiil ('repatriate' veya 'should repatriate') gelir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: When 'would rather' is followed by a different subject ('nineteenth-century colonial expeditions') referring to a past event, it requires the Past Perfect ('had not confiscated'). In the second blank, the mandative verb 'demanding that' triggers the present subjunctive bare infinitive ('repatriate').

distractorAnalysis.A: 'were not confiscating' expresses present ongoing preference rather than a completed 19th-century action.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'would not confiscate' is not used in the subordinate clause of 'would rather'.
distractorAnalysis.C: Correct: Past Perfect ('had not confiscated') for a counterfactual past preference after 'would rather', paired with bare infinitive ('repatriate') after 'demanding that'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'did not confiscate' after 'would rather + subject' refers to the present/future, conflicting with 'nineteenth-century', and 'repatriated' violates the mandative subjunctive.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'have not confiscated' cannot follow 'would rather', and 'should have repatriated' refers to the past rather than a current demand.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Expectation vs. Past Ability (Could Not Have V3)
grammarQuestions.stem: Even if early medieval scriptoria ---- access to cheaper linen parchment, literacy rates among the agrarian peasantry ---- substantially without a concurrent expansion of vernacular schooling.

options.A: would have / might not have risen
options.B: had had / could not have risen
options.C: were to have / would not have risen

cues: Even if + early medieval scriptoria (unreal past condition)
without ... (counterfactual past result)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Erken ortaçağ yazma eser atölyelerinin daha ucuz keten parşömene erişimi olmuş olsaydı bile, yerel dilde eğitimde eşzamanlı bir genişleme olmaksızın tarım köylüleri arasındaki okuryazarlık oranları önemli ölçüde artamazdı.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'early medieval scriptoria' (erken ortaçağ) geçmiş zamanı belirttiği için 'Even if' (Type 3 Unreal Past Conditional) yan cümleciğinde Past Perfect ('had had' - sahip olmuş olsaydı), ana cümlecikte ise geçmişteki imkansız sonucu ifade eden 'could not have risen' kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Because the sentence hypothesizes about 'early medieval scriptoria' (an unreal past scenario), the conditional clause requires the Past Perfect ('had had') and the main clause requires the past modal perfect ('could not have risen').

distractorAnalysis.A: 'would have' is generally disallowed in the conditional 'if' clause.
distractorAnalysis.B: Correct: 'had had' (Past Perfect of 'have') in the Type 3 'Even if' clause paired with 'could not have risen' in the main clause.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'were to have' is a Type 2 future/present hypothetical structure, incompatible with 'early medieval scriptoria'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'had / may not rise' forms a Type 2/mixed structure that fails to reflect the strictly past 'early medieval' timeframe.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'cannot rise' is a present modal that clashes with the medieval historical context.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Passive Perfect Participle & Passive Perfect Infinitive
grammarQuestions.stem: ---- in anaerobic peat bogs across Jutland for over two millennia, the Iron Age tollund bodies are reported ---- with such extraordinary dermal fidelity that forensic pathologists could reconstruct their final meals.

options.C: To be preserved / having been conserved
options.E: Having been preserved / to have been conserved

cues: by-agent/passive subject: 'the Iron Age tollund bodies'
for over two millennia (prior passive action)
are reported + passive perfect infinitive
grammarQuestions.translationTR: İki bin yılı aşkın bir süre boyunca Jutland genelindeki oksijensiz turba bataklıklarında korunmuş olan Demir Çağı bataklık cesetlerinin, adli patologların son öğünlerini yeniden yapılandırabileceği kadar olağanüstü bir deri bütünlüğüyle muhafaza edilmiş olduğu bildirilmektedir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: Ana cümlenin öznesi olan 'the Iron Age tollund bodies' (Demir Çağı cesetleri) koruma eylemini kendisi yapmadığından (edilgen) ve bu süreç ana fiilden önce gerçekleştiğinden ilk boşlukta Passive Perfect Participle ('Having been preserved') kullanılır. İkinci boşlukta ise edilgen çatıdaki 'are reported' fiilinden sonra geçmişteki edilgen durumu aktaran Passive Perfect Infinitive ('to have been conserved') gelmelidir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The subject 'the Iron Age tollund bodies' is the receiver of preservation over two millennia, requiring a passive perfect participial reduction ('Having been preserved'). Following the passive reporting verb 'are reported', a prior passive state requires the passive perfect infinitive ('to have been conserved').

distractorAnalysis.A: Both forms are active ('Having preserved / to have conserved'), violating the passive relationship with the subject.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'to conserve' is active, wrongly suggesting the bodies conserved something.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'having been conserved' (gerund) cannot follow the passive reporting structure 'are reported', which requires a 'to'-infinitive.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'Preserving' is active, creating a dangling participle as bodies do not preserve something else.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: 'Having been preserved' (passive perfect participle) + 'to have been conserved' (passive perfect infinitive after reporting verb).

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Superlative Infinitive Reduction & Active Participle
grammarQuestions.stem: PSR B1257+12 b, the first extrasolar planet ---- around a millisecond pulsar, startled astrophysicists by ---- within an intense radiation belt that should have stripped away any protoplanetary disk.
cues: the first + noun + passive to-infinitive
by + gerund (active: the planet orbits)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Bir milisaniye pulsarının etrafında tespit edilen ilk güneş dışı gezegen olan PSR B1257+12 b, herhangi bir ön-gezegen diskini yok etmiş olması gereken yoğun bir radyasyon kuşağı içinde yörüngede dönerek astrofizikçileri şaşkına çevirdi.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'the first, the second, the last, the only' gibi sıra sayı sıfatları ve superlative yapılardan sonra gelen relative clause kısaltmalarında 'to-infinitive' kullanılır; gezegen tespit edildiği (edilgen) için 'to be detected' (veya 'to have been detected') seçilir. İkinci boşlukta 'by' edatından sonra gezegenin kendisi yörüngede döndüğü için etken gerund ('orbiting') gelir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Ordinal and superlative phrases ('the first extrasolar planet') reduce relative clauses using a 'to'-infinitive; since the planet was detected by scientists, the passive infinitive 'to be detected' is required. After the preposition 'by', an active gerund ('orbiting') is needed.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'orbited' cannot directly follow the preposition 'by' as a verb form.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'having been orbited' is passive, whereas the planet actively orbits within the radiation belt.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'to orbit' cannot follow the preposition 'by'.
distractorAnalysis.D: Correct: Passive infinitive 'to be detected' after 'the first' + active gerund 'orbiting' after the preposition 'by'.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'to have detected' is active, implying the planet detected something else.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Causative Constructions & Passive Gerunds
grammarQuestions.stem: Before the titanium pressure hull could be certified for abyssal dives, the naval consortium had independent metallurgists ---- every weld seam by ultrasonic tomography to prevent the submersible from ---- to catastrophic implosion.
cues: had + [agent: independent metallurgists] + bare infinitive
prevent [object] from + passive gerund (being V3)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Titanyum basınç gövdesine derin deniz dalışları için sertifika verilmeden önce, denizcilik konsorsiyumu denizaltının yıkıcı bir içe patlamaya maruz kalmasını önlemek amacıyla bağımsız metalurjistlere her bir kaynak dikişini ultrasonik tomografiyle inceletti.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşlukta ettirgen (causative) yapı 'have + somebody (independent metallurgists) + do (V1)' kuralı gereği yalın fiil ('inspect') alır. İkinci boşlukta ise 'prevent ... from' kalıbındaki edattan sonra denizaltının içe patlamaya maruz bırakılması edilgen olduğundan Passive Gerund ('being subjected') kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The active causative pattern 'have + someone + bare infinitive' ('had independent metallurgists inspect') requires the base verb 'inspect'. In the second blank, the preposition 'from' requires a gerund, and because the submersible is the passive recipient of implosion forces, the passive gerund 'being subjected' is necessary.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'have sb to do' is ungrammatical (unlike 'get sb to do'), and 'having subjected' is active.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'be inspected' is ungrammatical after 'had metallurgists'.
distractorAnalysis.C: While 'have sb doing' exists in other contexts, 'to be subjected' cannot follow the preposition 'from'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'had ... inspected' is for passive objects ('had the seams inspected'), not active human agents ('independent metallurgists'); 'subjecting' is active.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: Bare infinitive 'inspect' in 'have sb do sth' + passive gerund 'being subjected' after 'from'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Passive Causative (Be Made To V1) & Participial Clause
grammarQuestions.stem: Under the draconian maritime statutes of 1651, foreign merchant vessels ---- their entire cargo manifests at English ports of entry, ---- continental intermediaries of their lucrative carrying trade.

options.A: were making to declare / to deprive
options.C: were made to declare / thereby depriving

cues: passive causative: be made + to V1
resultative active participle: thereby V-ing
grammarQuestions.translationTR: 1651 tarihli ağır denizcilik yasaları uyarınca, yabancı ticaret gemilerine tüm kargo manifestolarını İngiliz giriş limanlarında beyan etme zorunluluğu getirildi ve böylece kıta Avrupası'ndaki aracılar kazançlı taşımacılık ticaretinden mahrum bırakıldı.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: Etken çatıda 'make somebody do something' (yalın fiil) kullanılırken, bu yapı edilgen (passive) hale getirildiğinde 'be made TO do something' ('were made to declare') şeklinde 'to' alır. İkinci boşlukta ise ana cümlenin sonucunu bildiren etken zarf fiil kısaltması ('thereby depriving' = which thereby deprived) kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: When the causative verb 'make' is turned into the passive voice, it requires a full 'to'-infinitive ('were made to declare'). The second clause is a resultative participial reduction ('thereby depriving' = which thereby deprived).

distractorAnalysis.A: 'were making to declare' is not a valid English causative structure.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'made to declare' lacks a finite auxiliary verb for the main clause.
distractorAnalysis.C: Correct: Passive causative 'were made to declare' + resultative present participle 'thereby depriving'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'had made to declare' is grammatically ill-formed, and 'deprived' would wrongly modify the vessels as passive.
distractorAnalysis.E: Omits 'to' after passive 'were made' ('were made declare' is ungrammatical).

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Subordinate Conjunction + Participle Reduction
grammarQuestions.stem: Once ---- into the host cell's cytoplasm, the synthetic mRNA strand is translated by ribosomes into viral spike glycoproteins before ---- by intracellular exonucleases.
cues: Once + V3 (passive reduction of 'Once it is delivered')
before + being V3 (preposition/conjunction + passive gerund)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Konak hücrenin sitoplazmasına bir kez iletildiğinde, sentetik mRNA dizisi hücre içi ekzonükleazlar tarafından parçalanmadan önce ribozomlar tarafından viral başak glikoproteinlerine çevrilir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: Ana cümlenin öznesi 'the synthetic mRNA strand' (sentetik mRNA dizisi) hem iletilen hem de parçalanan konumundadır (her iki boşluk da edilgendir). 'Once' bağlacından sonra edilgen kısaltma olarak V3 ('Once delivered' = Once it is delivered), 'before' edat/bağlacından sonra ise edilgen gerund ('being degraded') kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The subject 'the synthetic mRNA strand' is passive in both actions: it is delivered into the cytoplasm ('Once delivered' = reduced from 'Once it is delivered') and is subsequently degraded by exonucleases ('before being degraded').

distractorAnalysis.A: Correct: 'Once delivered' (passive participle reduction) + 'before being degraded' (passive gerund).
distractorAnalysis.B: 'having delivered' is active, and 'to be degraded' cannot follow 'before'.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'having degraded' is active, conflicting with the passive agent 'by intracellular exonucleases'.
distractorAnalysis.D: Both 'delivering' and 'degrading' are active, wrongly implying the mRNA strand delivers and degrades something else.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'Once to be delivered' is not a valid participial reduction for a completed prerequisite.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Passive Reporting Verbs & Active Participles
grammarQuestions.stem: The Antikythera mechanism, widely believed ---- in a shipwreck off the Greek coast around 60 BCE, contains differential gear trains sophisticated enough ---- nineteenth-century clockmakers.

options.B: to be lost / to be astonished
options.C: to have been lost / to have astonished

cues: believed + passive perfect infinitive (around 60 BCE)
adjective + enough + to have V3 (nineteenth-century)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: MÖ 60 civarında Yunanistan kıyılarındaki bir gemi batığında kaybolduğuna yaygın olarak inanılan Antikythera düzeneği, 19. yüzyıl saat ustalarını hayrete düşürecek kadar gelişmiş diferansiyel dişli takımları içermektedir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: MÖ 60 yılında gerçekleşmiş edilgen bir olay ('around 60 BCE') 'believed' sıfat-fiilinden sonra Passive Perfect Infinitive ('to have been lost') ile aktarılır. İkinci boşlukta ise 'sophisticated enough + to-infinitive' kalıbı, 19. yüzyıldaki saatçileri etkileme (etken ve geçmişe dönük) anlamıyla 'to have astonished' alır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: After 'widely believed', a passive event dated to 'around 60 BCE' requires the passive perfect infinitive ('to have been lost'). After 'sophisticated enough', an active perfect infinitive ('to have astonished') links the mechanism's complexity to its impact on nineteenth-century clockmakers.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'to have lost' is active, and 'enough' cannot be followed by a gerund ('having astonished').
distractorAnalysis.B: 'to be astonished' is passive, wrongly suggesting the gear trains were astonished by clockmakers.
distractorAnalysis.C: Correct: 'to have been lost' (prior passive infinitive) + 'to have astonished' (prior active infinitive after 'enough').
distractorAnalysis.D: 'believed being lost' is ungrammatical.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'believed' requires a 'to'-infinitive ('believed to...'), and 'enough' also requires a 'to'-infinitive rather than 'astonishing'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Preposition + Passive Gerund vs. Causative Get
grammarQuestions.stem: In addition to ---- by prolonged hyperinflation, the Weimar treasury struggled to get international creditors ---- the punitive reparation installments mandated by the Treaty of Versailles.

options.D: to be eroded / to be rescheduled

cues: In addition to (preposition) + by-agent -> passive gerund
get + [active agent: creditors] + to V1
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Uzun süreli hiperenflasyon tarafından aşındırılmış olmasının yanı sıra, Weimar hazinesi uluslararası alacaklıları Versay Antlaşması'nın zorunlu kıldığı cezalandırıcı tazminat taksitlerini yeniden planlamaya ikna etmekte zorlandı.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'In addition to' ifadesindeki 'to' bir edattır (preposition) ve kendisinden sonra gerund (V-ing) alır; devamında 'by prolonged hyperinflation' bulunduğu için edilgen gerund ('having been eroded') gerekir. İkinci boşlukta ise 'get somebody TO do something' ettirgen yapısı nedeniyle 'to reschedule' kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: In 'In addition to', 'to' is a preposition requiring a gerund; the presence of 'by prolonged hyperinflation' necessitates the passive perfect gerund ('having been eroded'). In the second clause, the active causative 'get + person + to-infinitive' requires 'to reschedule'.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'rescheduled' (V3) would mean the creditors themselves were rescheduled rather than the creditors rescheduling the installments.
distractorAnalysis.B: Correct: Passive perfect gerund 'having been eroded' after preposition 'to' + 'to reschedule' in 'get sb to do sth'.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'eroding' is active despite the passive agent 'by prolonged hyperinflation', and 'get sb V1' omits the mandatory 'to'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'In addition to' cannot be followed by an infinitive ('to be eroded').
distractorAnalysis.E: 'having eroded' is active, and 'rescheduling' does not fit the persuasive causative 'get sb to do sth'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Absolute Participial Construction (With + Noun + Participle)
grammarQuestions.stem: With its primary Magneto-Optical Trap ---- by a sudden coolant leak, the quantum optics laboratory had no alternative but ---- the Bose-Einstein condensate experiment until replacement cryostats arrived.

options.A: to be compromised / to have postponed

cues: With + [noun] + V3 (by a sudden coolant leak)
have no alternative but + to V1
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Ana Manyeto-Optik Tuzağının ani bir soğutucu sızıntısı nedeniyle zarar görmesi üzerine, kuantum optik laboratuvarının yedek kriyostatlar gelene kadar Bose-Einstein yoğuşması deneyini ertelemekten başka seçeneği kalmadı.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'With + nesne + V3 / V-ing' (nominative absolute) yapısında 'by a sudden coolant leak' ifadesi tuzağın dış bir etkenle zarar gördüğünü (edilgen) gösterdiğinden V3 ('compromised') seçilir. İkinci boşlukta ise 'have no alternative/choice/option but to V1' kalıbı gereği 'to postpone' kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: In the absolute construction 'With + noun + participle', the phrase 'by a sudden coolant leak' indicates a passive relationship, requiring the past participle 'compromised'. The idiom 'have no alternative but' takes a 'to'-infinitive ('to postpone').

distractorAnalysis.A: 'to be compromised' expresses future purpose rather than the completed mishap that forced postponement.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'having postponed' cannot follow 'had no alternative but'.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'compromising' is active despite 'by a sudden coolant leak', and 'have no alternative but' takes a 'to'-infinitive rather than a gerund.
distractorAnalysis.D: Correct: Past participle 'compromised' in the passive 'With...' construction + 'to postpone' after 'had no alternative but'.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'having compromised' is active; also, after 'have no alternative but', 'to-infinitive' is standard when no 'do' verb precedes 'but'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Concessive 'Much as' vs. Causal 'Inasmuch as'
grammarQuestions.stem: ---- classical economists lauded the gold standard for enforcing fiscal discipline across trading nations, its rigid parity mechanisms prevented central banks from expanding liquidity during deflationary shocks.
cues: lauded (positive) vs. rigid ... prevented (negative)
Concession at the start of a full clause
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Klasik iktisatçılar altın standardını ticaret yapan uluslar arasında mali disiplini zorunlu kıldığı için ne kadar övmüş olurlarsa olsunlar (övmesine rağmen), onun katı parite mekanizmaları merkez bankalarının deflasyonist şoklar sırasında likiditeyi genişletmesini engelledi.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: Yan cümlecikteki 'lauded for enforcing fiscal discipline' (mali disiplini sağladığı için övdü - olumlu) ile ana cümlecikteki 'prevented central banks from expanding liquidity' (likiditeyi genişletmesini engelledi - olumsuz) arasında tam bir zıtlık/ödünleme (concession) vardır. Cümle başında 'Although / Even though' anlamında kullanılan 'Much as + SVO' yapısı bu zıtlığı sağlar.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The sentence contrasts classical economists' praise ('lauded') with a severe structural drawback ('prevented central banks from expanding liquidity'). 'Much as' functions as a formal concessive conjunction meaning 'Although / Even though'.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'So that' expresses purpose, contradicting the opposition between the two clauses.
distractorAnalysis.B: Correct: 'Much as' (= Although) introduces a concessive adverbial clause.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'Inasmuch as' means 'because / since' or 'to the extent that', which fails to express the contrast between praise and failure.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'Lest' means 'for fear that / in order that ... not', which does not fit a factual historical contrast.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'Provided that' introduces a strict condition ('only if'), which is semantically incongruent.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Negative Purpose ('Lest') vs. Causal Conjunctions
grammarQuestions.stem: Sixteenth-century Venetian glassmakers were strictly confined to the island of Murano under threat of capital punishment ---- they divulge proprietary chemical formulas for cristallo glass to rival European courts.
cues: confined ... under threat (precautionary measure)
they divulge (bare infinitive / subjunctive after lest)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: On altıncı yüzyıl Venedikli cam ustaları, cristallo camına ait gizli kimyasal formülleri rakip Avrupa saraylarına ifşa etmesinler diye (ifşa ederler korkusuyla) ölüm cezası tehdidi altında Murano adasına sıkı bir şekilde hapsedilmişlerdi.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İkinci cümlecikteki 'they divulge' ifadesinde geçmiş zaman bağlamına rağmen fiilin yalın halde (subjunctive / bare infinitive) kullanıldığına dikkat edilmelidir. 'Olmasın diye / ... korkusuyla' anlamına gelen ve kendisinden sonra 'should + V1' veya subjunctive yalın fiil ('divulge') alan bağlaç 'lest'tir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Notice the subjunctive bare verb 'divulge' (rather than 'divulged') in a sixteenth-century historical sentence. The conjunction 'lest' ('for fear that / in order that ... not') triggers the present subjunctive and explains the precautionary confinement.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'whereas' expresses direct contrast and would require the past tense 'divulged'.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'inasmuch as' ('since/because') neither fits the preventive meaning nor explains the bare subjunctive verb 'divulge'.
distractorAnalysis.C: Correct: 'lest' expresses negative purpose/precaution and grammatically licenses the subjunctive 'they divulge'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'as though' ('mış gibi') expresses manner/unreal comparison, not precautionary prohibition.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'now that' ('mademki / artık ... olduğuna göre') requires present/present perfect context and expresses cause.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Prepositional Concessive vs. Causal Connector
grammarQuestions.stem: ---- the proliferation of high-resolution satellite altimetry, bathymetrical maps of the abyssal ocean floor remain far less detailed than topographical charts of Mars, ---- the rapid attenuation of electromagnetic waves in seawater.

options.C: On account of / in spite of

cues: proliferation of satellite altimetry (advanced tech) vs. remain far less detailed (contrast)
rapid attenuation of waves in seawater (scientific cause)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Yüksek çözünürlüklü uydu altimetrisinin yaygınlaşmasına rağmen, derin okyanus tabanının batimetrik haritaları, elektromanyetik dalgaların deniz suyunda hızla zayıflaması yüzünden Mars'ın topografik haritalarından çok daha az ayrıntılı kalmaktadır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşlukta 'uydu teknolojisinin yaygınlaşması' ile 'okyanus tabanı haritalarının hâlâ az detaylı kalması' arasındaki zıtlığı vermek için '-e rağmen' anlamındaki 'Notwithstanding' (Despite/In spite of) kullanılır. İkinci boşlukta ise bu durumun bilimsel sebebini ('elektromanyetik dalgaların suda zayıflaması') açıklamak için '-den dolayı' anlamındaki 'owing to' gerekir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The first blank requires a concessive preposition ('Notwithstanding' = Despite) to contrast satellite advances with poor ocean-floor mapping. The second blank requires a causal prepositional phrase ('owing to' = because of) to explain the physical reason behind this limitation.

distractorAnalysis.A: Correct: 'Notwithstanding' (concession) + 'owing to' (cause).
distractorAnalysis.B: Reverses the logic: satellite proliferation is not the cause of poor detail, nor is wave attenuation a contrast.
distractorAnalysis.C: Reverses concession and cause ('On account of' = because of; 'in spite of' = despite).
distractorAnalysis.D: 'In pursuit of' ('peşinde') and 'regardless of' ('bakılmaksızın') distort the scientific cause-and-effect relationship.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'Prior to' (chronological) and 'contrary to' (contradiction) do not fit the physics explanation.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Albeit (Concessive Phrase) vs. Whereas (Direct Antithesis)
grammarQuestions.stem: The primordial atmosphere of Titan resembles that of early Earth in its dense nitrogen-methane composition, ---- at cryogenic surface temperatures, ---- Venus evolved a runaway greenhouse climate dominated by supercritical carbon dioxide.
cues: at cryogenic surface temperatures (verbless prepositional phrase -> albeit)
Titan ... vs. Venus ... (direct clause contrast -> whereas)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Titan'ın ilkel atmosferi, kriyojenik yüzey sıcaklıklarında olsa da, yoğun azot-metan bileşimi bakımından erken Dünya'nınkine benzer; oysa Venüs süperkritik karbondioksitin hâkim olduğu kontrolden çıkmış bir sera iklimi geliştirmiştir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşluktan sonra tam bir cümle (SVO) değil, edat öbeği ('at cryogenic surface temperatures') gelmektedir; fiilsiz sıfat/zarf/edat öbekleriyle 'olsa da / gerçi' anlamında kullanılan bağlaç 'albeit'tir. İkinci boşlukta ise Titan ile Venüs arasındaki doğrudan taban tabana zıtlığı (antitez) kurmak için 'whereas' (oysaki / -iken) kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The first blank precedes a verbless prepositional phrase ('at cryogenic surface temperatures'), where 'albeit' ('although it is') is uniquely grammatical. The second blank contrasts two full clauses comparing Titan and Venus, requiring 'whereas'.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'forasmuch as' requires a full finite clause, and 'unless' introduces a condition.
distractorAnalysis.B: Correct: 'albeit' before a reduced modifier phrase + 'whereas' for direct antithesis between Titan and Venus.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'even though' typically requires a finite verb or participial clause, and 'so that' expresses purpose.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'however' cannot link a prepositional modifier inside a clause without punctuation in this way.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'despite' requires a noun phrase/gerund (not a 'preposition + noun' phrase like 'at temperatures'), and 'whereby' means 'by which'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Just As ... So Too (Correlative Analogy)
grammarQuestions.stem: ---- the printing press dismantled the clerical monopoly over scriptural exegesis in sixteenth-century Europe, ---- decentralized cryptographic protocols are now challenging the intermediation of sovereign central banks.
cues: Historical parallel between 16th-century printing press and modern cryptographic protocols
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Tıpkı matbaanın on altıncı yüzyıl Avrupası'nda kutsal metin tefsiri üzerindeki ruhban sınıfı tekelini yıkması gibi, merkeziyetsiz kriptografik protokoller de günümüzde egemen merkez bankalarının aracılık rolüne meydan okumaktadır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İki farklı tarihsel olgu (16. yüzyılda matbaanın ruhban tekelini yıkması ile günümüzde kriptografik protokollerin merkez bankalarına meydan okuması) arasında 'tıpkı ... olduğu gibi, ... da öyledir' şeklinde analoji (benzeşim) kuran korelatif bağlaç çifti 'Just as ... so (too)' yapısıdır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: To draw a structural analogy between two parallel historical transformations, academic English uses the correlative pair 'Just as [Clause A], so too [Clause B]'.

distractorAnalysis.A: If 'Not only' were placed at the beginning of the first clause, it would require auxiliary inversion ('Not only did the printing press dismantle...').
distractorAnalysis.B: 'Scarcely ... when' requires past perfect inversion and describes immediate temporal succession.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'Whether ... or' expresses alternative possibilities rather than historical analogy.
distractorAnalysis.D: Correct: 'Just as ... so too' establishes a parallel analogy without requiring inversion in the first clause.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'No sooner ... than' requires past perfect inversion and temporal immediacy.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Insofar As / Inasmuch As (Degree & Justification)
grammarQuestions.stem: International maritime tribunals recognize a coastal state's exclusive economic zone over continental shelf resources only ---- those geological formations constitute a natural prolongation of its land territory.
cues: only ---- (restrictive extent/degree)
constitute a natural prolongation (criterion)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Uluslararası deniz hukuku mahkemeleri, bir kıyı devletinin kıta sahanlığı kaynakları üzerindeki münhasır ekonomik bölgesini yalnızca bu jeolojik oluşumların kara ülkesinin doğal bir uzantısını teşkil ettiği ölçüde tanır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: Boşluktan önceki 'only' zarfıyla birleşerek 'yalnızca ... ölçüde / ...-dığı kadarıyla' anlamında kısıtlayıcı bir koşul ve derece bildiren akademik bağlaç 'insofar as' (veya 'inasmuch as') yapısıdır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Preceded by 'only', the conjunction 'insofar as' ('to the extent that') specifies the exact legal and geological degree to which a coastal state's jurisdiction is recognized.

distractorAnalysis.A: Correct: 'only insofar as' means 'only to the extent that'.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'as though' expresses hypothetical comparison.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'for fear that' expresses negative precaution, which makes no sense after 'only'.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'regardless of' is a prepositional phrase requiring a noun/nominal clause, not a finite 'those formations constitute' clause.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'only even if' is a contradictory combination of restriction and concession.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: No Matter How + Adj/Adv vs. Whatever + Noun
grammarQuestions.stem: ---- meticulously a quantum key distribution network is shielded against fiber-optic eavesdropping, side-channel vulnerabilities in photon detectors can still be exploited ---- hardware calibration protocols are continuously updated.
cues: ---- meticulously (adverb immediately after blank)
can still be exploited ---- (negative exception -> unless)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Bir kuantum anahtar dağıtım ağı fiber optik dinlemeye karşı ne kadar titizlikle korunursa korunsun, donanım kalibrasyon protokolleri sürekli güncellenmediği sürece foton dedektörlerindeki yan kanal güvenlik açıkları yine de istismar edilebilir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşluktan hemen sonra bir zarf ('meticulously') geldiği için 'ne kadar ... olursa olsun' anlamında 'No matter how + adj/adv' veya 'However + adj/adv' kullanılmalıdır. İkinci boşlukta ise 'donanım protokolleri güncellenmediği sürece açıklar istismar edilebilir' anlamını veren 'unless' (if ... not) doğru eşleşmeyi sağlar.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Because the word immediately following the first blank is the adverb 'meticulously', 'No matter how' (or 'However') is required. The second blank requires 'unless' ('except if') to state the necessary condition to prevent exploitation.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'Whatever' cannot modify the adverb 'meticulously' (it modifies nouns or functions as a pronoun).
distractorAnalysis.B: 'Much as' modifies a whole clause rather than intensifying the adverb 'meticulously', and 'so that' is wrong in the second blank.
distractorAnalysis.C: While 'However meticulously' is grammatical for the first blank, 'in case' ('olur diye') destroys the logic of the second clause.
distractorAnalysis.D: Correct: 'No matter how + adverb (meticulously)' + 'unless' (negative condition).
distractorAnalysis.E: 'Regardless of' is a preposition and cannot be followed directly by an adverb + finite clause.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: In the Wake Of vs. At the Expense Of
grammarQuestions.stem: ---- the catastrophic 1953 North Sea storm surge, the Dutch parliament commissioned the Delta Works, prioritizing long-term estuarine flood defense ---- short-term agricultural and navigational convenience.

options.A: On behalf of / for the sake of
options.B: By means of / in compliance with
options.C: In lieu of / by virtue of
options.D: With respect to / in accordance with
options.E: In the wake of / at the expense of

cues: 1953 storm surge -> Delta Works commissioned (aftermath)
prioritizing A ---- B (sacrificing B for A)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Yıkıcı 1953 Kuzey Denizi fırtına kabarmasının hemen ardından (artçı etkisiyle), Hollanda parlamentosu kısa vadeli tarımsal ve denizcilik kolaylığı pahasına uzun vadeli haliç taşkın savunmasına öncelik vererek Delta Çalışmaları'nı başlattı.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşlukta 1953 felaketinin 'hemen ardından / sonucunda' anlamını veren 'In the wake of' kullanılır. İkinci boşlukta ise bir şeye diğerinin 'pahasına / zararına' öncelik verildiğini anlatan 'at the expense of' edat öbeği tam anlam bütünlüğü sağlar.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: 'In the wake of' means 'following closely after / as a consequence of' a major event (the 1953 disaster). 'At the expense of' pairs naturally with 'prioritizing' to show what was sacrificed ('short-term convenience').

distractorAnalysis.A: 'On behalf of' ('namına/temsilen') cannot be used with a storm surge.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'By means of' (instrument) and 'in compliance with' (obedience) do not fit a natural disaster or a policy trade-off.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'In lieu of' ('yerine') makes no sense before a storm surge.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'With respect to' and 'in accordance with' fail to capture the chronological cause and the policy trade-off.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: 'In the wake of' (in the aftermath of) + 'at the expense of' (sacrificing).

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Causal Framing (Given That) & Discourse Result (Hence)
grammarQuestions.stem: ---- lithium-ion electrolytes undergo rapid dendritic crystallization at sub-zero temperatures, conventional battery packs lose up to forty percent of their discharge capacity in polar environments; ----, arctic autonomous rovers require solid-state thermal management.
cues: undergo crystallization -> lose 40% capacity (cause -> effect)
; ----, require thermal management (logical conclusion)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Lityum-iyon elektrolitlerin sıfırın altındaki sıcaklıklarda hızlı dendritik kristalleşmeye uğradığı göz önüne alındığında, geleneksel batarya paketleri kutup ortamlarında deşarj kapasitelerinin yüzde kırkına kadarını kaybeder; bu yüzden Arktik otonom keşif araçları katı hal ısıl yönetimine ihtiyaç duyar.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk cümlecik kapasite kaybının bilimsel nedenini ortaya koyduğu için 'Given that' (göz önüne alındığında / -dığı için) bağlacını alır. Noktalı virgülden sonraki cümle ise bu sorunun mühendislik sonucunu ('bu nedenle / dolayısıyla') ifade ettiğinden 'hence' geçiş zarfını gerektirir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: 'Given that' introduces the known scientific premise causing capacity loss, while the conjunctive adverb 'hence' ('therefore / consequently') introduces the engineering necessity that follows after the semicolon.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'Provided that' ('koşuluyla') and 'instead' ('bunun yerine') distort the scientific logic.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'Whereas' and 'otherwise' do not fit the causal chain.
distractorAnalysis.C: Correct: 'Given that' (premise/cause) + 'hence' (logical consequence).
distractorAnalysis.D: 'Even though' and 'conversely' wrongly frame a direct chain of cause and effect as two contradictions.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'Unless' turns a factual chemical property into a negative condition, and 'nevertheless' expresses concession rather than result.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Compound Conditionals (On Condition That vs. Only If)
grammarQuestions.stem: The central bank agreed to extend emergency liquidity facilities to insolvent commercial lenders ---- they divested their speculative sovereign debt portfolios and suspended executive dividend payouts.
cues: agreed to extend ... ---- they divested (strict stipulation/prerequisite)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Merkez bankası, ödeme güçlüğündeki ticari kredi kuruluşlarına, spekülatif devlet tahvili portföylerini elden çıkarmaları ve yönetici temettü ödemelerini askıya almaları şartıyla acil likidite olanaklarını uzatmayı kabul etti.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'agreed to extend ...' (uzatmayı kabul etti) ifadesinden sonra bankaların yerine getirmesi gereken katı sözleşme şartları sıralanmaktadır. '-mesi şartıyla / koşuluyla' anlamına gelen 'on condition that' (provided that) bu hukuki ve finansal koşulu tam olarak karşılar.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: 'on condition that' introduces a strict stipulation required for the central bank's agreement to provide emergency liquidity.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'for fear that' expresses negative purpose, reversing the intended meaning.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'in contrast to' is a preposition and cannot precede a finite clause ('they divested...').
distractorAnalysis.C: 'even if' ('olsa bile') implies the central bank would lend regardless of reform, which contradicts regulatory logic.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'as though' ('-mış gibi') expresses manner or unreal comparison.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: 'on condition that' introduces the binding prerequisite for the bailout.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Quantifier Relative Clauses & Interrogative Noun Clauses
grammarQuestions.stem: The archaeological mission cataloged over three hundred Urartian bronze belts, ---- bore incised mythological friezes, yet scholars remain divided over ---- these motifs served apotropaic or purely dynastic functions.
cues: comma + quantifier + of + relative pronoun (inanimate: bronze belts)
divided over ---- ... or ... (whether ... or)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Arkeoloji heyeti, birçoğu kazıma mitolojik frizler taşıyan üç yüzden fazla Urartu bronz kemerini katalogladı; ancak araştırmacılar bu motiflerin kötülük savıcı mı yoksa salt hanedanlık işlevi mi gördüğü konusunda hâlâ ikiye bölünmüş durumdadır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşlukta virgülden sonra gelen ve cansız bir öncülü ('three hundred Urartian bronze belts') niteleyen miktar ifadeli relative clause yapısı 'many of which' gerektirir ('most of them' bağlaçsız iki cümleyi virgüle bağlayamaz - comma splice). İkinci boşlukta ise 'divided over' (konusunda bölünmüş) ve devamındaki 'or' ipucu nedeniyle 'olup olmadığı' anlamındaki noun clause bağlacı 'whether' kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Joining two finite clauses with a comma requires a relative pronoun ('many of which', referring to inanimate 'bronze belts') rather than a personal pronoun ('them'). In the second blank, 'divided over ... or ...' requires the noun clause subordinator 'whether' (note that 'if' cannot follow a preposition like 'over').

distractorAnalysis.A: 'which' in the second blank is redundant because 'these motifs' already has the determiner 'these'.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'most of them' creates a comma splice error without a conjunction, and 'that' cannot follow the preposition 'over'.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'all of whose' requires a noun immediately after 'whose', not the finite verb 'bore'.
distractorAnalysis.D: Correct: 'many of which' (non-defining quantifier relative clause) + 'whether' (noun clause object of the preposition 'over' paired with 'or').
distractorAnalysis.E: 'whom' refers only to human antecedents, not 'bronze belts'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Preposition + Relative Pronoun ('Whereby / By Which') vs. Nominal 'What'
grammarQuestions.stem: Epigenetics investigates the biochemical mechanisms ---- environmental stressors alter gene expression without mutating the underlying DNA sequence, fundamentally redefining ---- evolutionary biologists mean by heritable variation.
cues: mechanisms [by which] stressors alter ... (complete SVO clause)
redefining ---- biologists mean (missing object of 'mean')
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Epigenetik, çevresel stres faktörlerinin altta yatan DNA dizisini mutasyona uğratmadan gen ifadesini değiştirdiği biyokimyasal mekanizmaları araştırır ve evrimsel biyologların kalıtsal çeşitlilik ile neyi kastettiğini temelden yeniden tanımlar.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşluktan sonraki cümlecik ('environmental stressors alter gene expression') özne ve nesnesi tam bir cümledir; 'the mechanisms by which' (aracılığıyla / sayesinde değiştirdiği mekanizmalar - 'whereby' eşdeğeri) gerekir. İkinci boşlukta ise 'redefining' fiilinin nesnesi olan ve aynı zamanda 'mean' fiilinin eksik nesnesini karşılayan 'what' (şey / neyi) noun clause zamiri kullanılmalıdır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: Because 'environmental stressors alter gene expression' is already a syntactically complete SVO clause, modifying 'the biochemical mechanisms' requires the instrumental relative 'by which' (or 'whereby'). In the second blank, 'mean' lacks a direct object, requiring the fused relative/nominal pronoun 'what' ('that which').

distractorAnalysis.A: 'which' alone cannot link 'mechanisms' to a complete SVO clause without a preposition, and 'that' cannot provide the missing object of 'mean'.
distractorAnalysis.B: Correct: 'by which' (instrumental relative pronoun modifying 'mechanisms') + 'what' (nominal pronoun serving as object of both 'redefining' and 'mean').
distractorAnalysis.C: 'how' after 'redefining ... mean' would mean 'how biologists mean', which is unidiomatic ('mean' takes 'what', not 'how').
distractorAnalysis.D: 'whose' requires a possessed noun without an article, not 'environmental stressors'.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'in that' means 'inasmuch as / because' and does not modify 'mechanisms'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Possessive Relative 'Whose' & Appositive Noun Clause 'That'
grammarQuestions.stem: The cosmic microwave background radiation, ---- temperature anisotropies were mapped with micro-kelvin precision by the Planck spacecraft, lent decisive empirical support to the hypothesis ---- the nascent universe underwent exponential inflationary expansion.
cues: comma + ---- + bare noun phrase ('temperature anisotropies')
the hypothesis ---- + complete statement (appositive noun clause)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Sıcaklık anizotropileri Planck uzay aracı tarafından mikro-kelvin hassasiyetiyle haritalandırılan kozmik mikrodalga arka plan ışıması, erken evrenin üstel şişme (enflasyon) genişlemesi geçirdiği hipotezine kesin ampirik destek sağlamıştır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşluktan sonra artikelsiz bir isim tamlaması ('temperature anisotropies' - ışımanın sıcaklık anizotropileri) geldiği için sahiplik bildiren relative zamiri 'whose' kullanılır (cansız varlıklar için de kullanılır). İkinci boşlukta ise 'the hypothesis' soyut isminin içeriğini tam bir cümleyle açıklayan appositive noun clause bağlacı 'that' gerekir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: In the first blank, 'temperature anisotropies' belongs to 'the cosmic microwave background radiation' and lacks a determiner, requiring the possessive relative pronoun 'whose'. In the second blank, 'the hypothesis' takes an appositive content clause introduced by 'that'.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'where' cannot modify 'temperature anisotropies' as a possessive, and 'whether' implies uncertainty contradicting 'decisive empirical support'.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'that' cannot be used after a comma in a non-defining relative clause.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'which' cannot precede a bare noun ('temperature anisotropies') without a verb or preposition, and 'which' in the second blank would leave 'hypothesis' unexpressed in the relative clause.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'of which' requires the definite article ('the temperature anisotropies of which'), and 'what' cannot introduce an appositive clause after a complete SVO.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: 'whose' (possessive relative) + 'that' (appositive noun clause complement to 'the hypothesis').

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Subjunctive Mandative Noun Clause & 'Whatever' Determiner
grammarQuestions.stem: The Basel Committee's regulatory framework stipulates ---- systemically important financial institutions maintain sufficient Tier-1 capital buffers to absorb ---- macroeconomic shocks may arise from sovereign defaults.
cues: stipulates ---- + complete mandative clause ('institutions maintain')
absorb ---- macroeconomic shocks (nominal determiner before plural noun)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Basel Komitesi'nin düzenleyici çerçevesi, sistemik olarak önemli finansal kuruluşların devlet temerrütlerinden kaynaklanabilecek her türlü makroekonomik şoku emmek için yeterli Çekirdek-1 sermaye tamponunu bulundurmasını şart koşmaktadır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: İlk boşlukta 'stipulate' (şart koşmak) fiilinin nesnesi olan tam cümleyi bağlamak için 'that' kullanılır. İkinci boşlukta ise açık uçlu bir isim öbeğini ('macroeconomic shocks') niteleyen ve 'ne tür / hangi makroekonomik şoklar ortaya çıkarsa çıksın' anlamını veren 'whatever + noun' yapısı doğru seçimdir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The verb 'stipulates' takes a declarative content clause headed by 'that'. In the second blank, 'whatever' functions as a relative determiner modifying the noun phrase 'macroeconomic shocks' ('any macroeconomic shocks that may arise').

distractorAnalysis.A: 'what' cannot introduce a complete clause after 'stipulates', and 'whichever' implies a restricted choice from a predefined set.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'which' cannot introduce a declarative noun clause after 'stipulates', and 'whenever' is a temporal adverb rather than a nominal determiner for 'shocks'.
distractorAnalysis.C: Correct: 'that' (noun clause complement of 'stipulates') + 'whatever' (indefinite relative determiner modifying 'macroeconomic shocks').
distractorAnalysis.D: 'whether' introduces doubt, contradicting a binding regulatory stipulation, and 'however' modifies adjectives/adverbs rather than nouns.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'whoever' refers to people, not 'macroeconomic shocks'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Prepositional Nominal Clauses ('In That' vs. 'To What Extent')
grammarQuestions.stem: Quasi-crystalline alloys differ fundamentally from conventional metallic lattices ---- their atomic arrangements exhibit long-range orientational order without periodic translational symmetry, raising intriguing questions as to ---- they conduct thermal energy.
cues: differ fundamentally ... ---- (specifying the exact respect/reason -> in that)
questions as to ---- they conduct thermal energy (manner)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Yarı-kristal alaşımlar, atomik dizilimlerinin periyodik öteleme simetrisi olmaksızın uzun menzilli yönelimsel düzen sergilemesi bakımından geleneksel metalik örgülerden temelden ayrılır; bu da onların ısı enerjisini nasıl ilettiklerine dair ilgi çekici sorular doğurmaktadır.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'differ from ... in that ...' kalıbında 'in that' bağlacı 'şu bakımdan ki / -mesi bakımından' anlamında farkın hangi noktada ortaya çıktığını açıklar. İkinci boşlukta ise 'as to' (hakkında / dair) edatından sonra ısı enerjisini 'nasıl' ilettiklerini soran noun clause zarfı 'how' gelir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: After 'differ ... from ...', the compound subordinator 'in that' ('inasmuch as / in the respect that') specifies the exact nature of the difference. After 'questions as to', the manner adverbial 'how' introduces an indirect question.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'given that' expresses a presupposed cause rather than specifying the dimension of difference.
distractorAnalysis.B: 'except that' expresses an exception to a general similarity rather than defining a fundamental difference.
distractorAnalysis.C: 'what' cannot fit 'they conduct thermal energy' because 'conduct' already has its direct object ('thermal energy').
distractorAnalysis.D: 'in which' would function as a relative clause modifying 'lattices' only, leaving 'differ fundamentally' unexplained.
distractorAnalysis.E: Correct: 'in that' ('in the respect that') + 'how' (interrogative noun clause of manner).

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Pseudo-Cleft Subject Noun Clause ('What ... Is That')
grammarQuestions.stem: ---- distinguishes the Cambrian explosion from earlier Ediacaran radiations is not merely the sudden proliferation of biomineralized exoskeletons, but ---- predatory-prey arms races drove rapid ecological niche partitioning.
cues: ---- distinguishes ... is (missing subject of 'distinguishes' + subject of 'is')
not merely [Noun Phrase], but ---- [complete SVO clause]
grammarQuestions.translationTR: Kambriyen patlamasını daha önceki Ediakara yayılımlarından ayıran şey, yalnızca biyomineralize dış iskeletlerin ani çoğalması değil, avcı-av silahlanma yarışlarının hızlı ekolojik niş bölünmesini tetiklemiş olması gerçeğidir.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: Cümlenin başında hem 'distinguishes' fiilinin öznesi olan hem de ana fiil 'is' için özne öbeği oluşturan yapı 'What' (Ayıran şey) zamiridir. İkinci kısımda ise 'not merely [the sudden proliferation...], but [the fact that + SVO]' paralel yapısında tam bir cümleyi isimleştirerek ilk isim öbeğine paralel kılan 'the fact that' (veya 'that') kullanılır.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: In a pseudo-cleft sentence where the verb 'distinguishes' lacks a subject, 'What' ('The thing that') is required. After 'not merely [NP], but...', 'the fact that' nominalizes the complete clause 'predatory-prey arms races drove...' to maintain parallelism with the first noun phrase.

distractorAnalysis.A: 'That' cannot serve as the subject of 'distinguishes' inside the noun clause, and 'what' cannot precede a complete SVO clause ('arms races drove partitioning').
distractorAnalysis.B: Correct: 'What' (fused relative subject) + 'the fact that' (nominalizer introducing a complete clause).
distractorAnalysis.C: 'Which' cannot introduce a subject noun clause without a noun or choice context.
distractorAnalysis.D: 'Whatever' is overly indefinite for a specific paleontological distinction.
distractorAnalysis.E: 'How' cannot serve as the grammatical subject of 'distinguishes'.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Adjective + Preposition Collocations (Tantamount To / Devoid Of)
grammarQuestions.stem: For nineteenth-century philologists, dismissing oral epic traditions as mere folklore was tantamount ---- erasing the formative centuries of archaic literacy, even when those ballads were devoid ---- verifiable chronological markers.
cues: tantamount + to + V-ing (equivalent to)
devoid + of + noun (completely lacking in)
grammarQuestions.translationTR: On dokuzuncu yüzyıl filologları için sözlü destan geleneklerini salt folklor olarak görmezden gelmek, bu baladlar doğrulanabilir kronolojik işaretlerden yoksun olduğunda bile arkaik okuryazarlığın kurucu yüzyıllarını silmekle eşdeğerdi.
grammarQuestions.explanationTR: 'tantamount to' (-e eşdeğer / denk) kalıbındaki 'to' bir edattır ve kendisinden sonra isim veya gerund ('erasing') alır. İkinci boşlukta ise 'devoid of' (-den tamamen yoksun / mahrum) kalıplaşmış sıfat+edat eşleşmesidir.
grammarQuestions.explanationEN: The adjective 'tantamount' always collocates with the preposition 'to' (+ noun/gerund), meaning 'equivalent to'. The adjective 'devoid' obligatorily collocates with 'of', meaning 'entirely lacking'.

distractorAnalysis.A: Correct: 'tantamount to' + 'devoid of'.
distractorAnalysis.B: Incorrect prepositional collocations.
distractorAnalysis.C: Incorrect prepositional collocations.
distractorAnalysis.D: Neither 'tantamount with' nor 'devoid from' is idiomatic in English.
distractorAnalysis.E: Incorrect prepositional collocations.

grammarQuestions.subtopic: Academic Phrasal Verbs (Account For / Stem From)
grammarQuestions.stem: Although dark baryonic matter such as brown dwarfs and rogue planets can only ---- a negligible fraction of the missing mass in galactic halos, the gravitational anomalies observed in spiral rotation curves must ---- non-baryonic particles or modified inertia.

options.E: do away with / fall back on

cues: a negligible fraction of the missing mass (explain/constitute -> account for)
